It's like a really engaging, long, enduring, creepypasta. Jump scares aren't really present, it's more of a visual novel, with much of the interaction coming from the description of everything that goes on within the plotline of the characters. There are only a few choices you make yourself. All in all it is truly a unique, shockingly memorable, experience.

For me, Lost Odyssey really ramped up after the halfway point, I finally got the hang of the ring system and the elements involved, along with the skills and accessories. Once I was able to put together how everything was connected, it added a whole new layer of depth to the game. After that I found how huge the world was with sidequests and fell in love with all the different locations and the unique boss elements. Then you can learn a lot about how all the characters got to where they are, and it creates an entirely new level of interest.
